summary: For 5–7 year-olds, establish a clear mental picture of a volcano: an opening in Earth's surface where hot melted rock (lava) comes out. The single most important idea is that lava is ROCK so hot it has melted and glows because of its heat — not fire, not a burning flame, and not some separate special liquid different from rock. Keep the work definitional (recognise, name, describe); defer magma chambers, vents, plate boundaries and eruption mechanism to later (7–9) topics. Build from vivid real imagery and a simple three-part labelled cross-section, and give children sentence frames to narrate what they see.
misconceptions: 'The glowing lava is fire' — it is rock so hot it has melted and glows; there is no burning flame in the flow
'A volcano is a mountain that breathes fire / a fire-breathing monster' — it is an opening in Earth's surface where melted rock comes out
'All volcanoes are tall pointed mountains' — the defining feature is the opening, not the cone shape
'Lava comes straight from the centre of the Earth' — at this age keep it to 'from hot melted rock underground'; deep structure comes later
'Volcanoes only existed long ago / are not real now' — many volcanoes are active today

activities.title: Tap-and-name the volcano picture
steps: Look at a large, friendly cross-section of an erupting volcano (mountain, opening at the top, lava flowing down, ash cloud).
Tap each part to hear/read a short naming phrase: 'the mountain', 'the opening at the top', 'the lava coming out', 'the ash cloud (tiny bits of rock, not ash from burning)'.
Open a lift-the-flap sitting on the lava: front asks 'What is lava?', the flap reveals 'Rock so hot it has MELTED — it glows because it is hot, it is not fire.'
Zoom in on a close-up where a blob of glowing orange lava cools and hardens into solid black rock.
Narrate the whole picture aloud using a sentence frame: 'The hot melted rock — lava — is coming out of the opening.'
activities.insight: A volcano is an opening where hot melted rock comes out; lava is rock that has melted and glows because it is so hot, and it cools back into solid rock.

activities.title: Press to erupt
steps: Tap the volcano to make it erupt: watch lava well up at the opening and flow down the sides.
Watch the lava cool from bright orange at the top to solid black rock at the cooled edges.
Read the caption that names the flowing stuff 'lava'.
Say in your own words where the lava is coming out and what happens as it cools.
activities.insight: Hot melted rock comes OUT of the opening of a volcano, and as it flows away and cools it hardens into solid rock.

activities.title: Melt-and-cool prediction (hands-on check)
steps: Look at a solid piece of wax or chocolate.

Before anything happens, PREDICT: if we heat it until it flows like lava and then let it cool, will it (a) burn up into ash, (b) turn into fire, or (c) become solid again — and say WHY. (Then we test it to see what really happens.)
An adult gently warms it (for example in a bowl over warm water, away from any flame) until it flows, then let it cool, and check what actually happens.

Connect it back: like lava, a hot melted solid can flow while it is hot and then harden back into a solid when it cools. Lava is far hotter, so lava also glows; the wax or chocolate is not hot enough to glow.

Answer the probes: 'If the glowing lava cools right down, what does it turn into?', 'Where does the melted rock come from — the top of the mountain, or from hot melted rock underground?', and 'Is the volcano hot because something is burning, or for a different reason?'
activities.insight: Glowing and hot does not mean burning: a melted solid flows while hot and hardens again when cooled, just as lava (melted rock) cools into solid rock. The wax/chocolate shows melting and re-solidifying; the glow is a feature of lava's extreme heat, not of the stand-in.

activities.title: Quick recognition check
steps: Choose from pictures: 'Which picture shows a volcano?'
Answer 'What is lava?' choosing from melted rock / fire / water (melted rock is correct).
Respond to a friend who says 'That's fire coming out of the mountain' — agree or disagree, and say what the orange stuff really is and where it comes from.
activities.insight: Confirm the child can recognise a volcano and state that lava is melted rock, not fire or water.

checkQuestion: This picture shows a volcano with glowing orange stuff pouring down it. A friend says, 'That's fire coming out of the mountain.' Do you agree? What is the orange stuff really, and where does it come from?
checkAnswer: The friend is wrong — it isn't fire. It's lava: rock from deep inside the Earth that got so hot it melted into a runny, glowing liquid. A volcano is an opening where this hot melted rock comes out, and when lava cools it turns back into hard rock.
